plos-pone-0003470: Data scientists raced prediction methods for HIV treatment in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003570: Microbiologists tested bacterial compartments as enzyme vaults in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0357570: Emergency department nurses work the hardest shifts in the hospital — and many are thinking of quitting. plos-pone-0357270: A little radiation can be a stimulant: this paper tested moderate gamma irradiation on humic acid, a natural soil booster, and applied it to tomatoes. plos-pone-0354870: Children of diabetic mothers inherit metabolic risk — and the hormone asprosin may be a messenger. plos-pone-0357770: Mobile robots need paths through messy, unpredictable real worlds. This paper fused improved BI-RRT with enhanced DWA for hybrid path planning in complex environments. The combination plans routes globally yet dodges obstacles locally — the best of both navigation worlds.
plos-pone-0357470: Why do some people react intensely to everything while others stay placid? plos-pone-0357970: ‘Forever chemicals’ may be quietly harming livers. plos-pone-0355370: Muscle building is choreographed by tiny RNA molecules pulling hidden strings. plos-pone-0357670: Long COVID’s PASC index attempts to track the syndrome’s shifting symptoms over time. This paper studied the kinetics of the index — how it rises, falls, and evolves in patients. The trajectories help define the condition’s natural course and give researchers a measurable target.
plos-pone-0357370: What Americans dreamed on election night predicted how they’d feel by morning. plos-pone-0356070: Psychology’s replication crisis demands better measurement, not just more studies. plos-pone-0337870: Knee braces that correct bow-legged gait need precise tuning. plos-pone-0356870: Pavement cracks hide in noisy, low-contrast road images. plos-pone-0356770: The gut microbiome may whisper to the thyroid — even in cancer. plos-pone-0356370: After birth, pinning down a newborn’s gestational age matters enormously — and the cerebellum holds clues. plos-pone-0328670: Stimulating the vagus nerve through the ear might calm functional dyspepsia — via immune reprogramming. plos-pone-0356270: Sleep disorders need reliable questionnaires — in every language. plos-pone-0349170: Bangladesh’s coastal ecosystems — mangroves, mudflats, estuaries — are under mounting pressure. plos-pone-0354270: Lakes’ oxygen patterns shape everything living in them. This paper showed spatial patterns of oxygen states affect lake food web structure through the response of cold-water fish. plos-pone-0356170: Predicting cardiovascular disease with machine learning has attracted dozens of competing techniques. This paper compared them head-to-head. plos-pone-0356470: Elderly feet need specialized nursing care — starting with nurses who know, care, and act. plos-pone-0355470: Studying how social networks evolve in virtual reality opens new windows on group dynamics. europmc-pmc2796170: Why do some gut bacteria take hold while others fail? europmc-pmc2815670: Solving protein structures from X-ray data takes a whole pipeline of programs, and this 2010 paper introduces the one that unified them. europmc-pmc2911870: Aching joints might be read in tiny RNAs. This 2010 paper tests microRNAs from blood and joint fluid as early flags of rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. The authors' picks could spot disease sooner. Their work points to blood tests for sore joints.

europmc-pmc6727070: Pneumonia is the top killer of young children - yet its causes in Africa and Asia were murky. pmc-13445770: A 2026 multi-level analysis of Trop-2 expression and its clinical significance in breast cancer — protein, transcript, and clinical levels (the title is truncated). The target's significance was mapped. The analysis guides antibody-drug conjugate therapy.
pmc-13462070: A 2026 microbiology paper: MarA bound and activated the ABC efflux pump YadGH to confer conditional macrolide resistance in AcrB-deficient E. coli. The backup pump's regulation was decoded. The conferring is the resistance mechanism.
pmc-13424770: This 2026 stroke imaging paper tested cardiac photon-counting detector CT's diagnostic accuracy for detecting left atrial appendage thrombus in acute ischemic stroke. The new CT's clot detection was validated. The accuracy is the evidence.
pmc-13421270: A 2026 music cognition paper: duration, but not intensity cues, facilitated synchronization to complex rhythms. The timing beat the loudness. The facilitating is the perceptual insight.
arxiv-2606-15970: A theory paper that proves a 'no-go' result: it pins down just how far a set of math tools (conormal invariants) can go in grasping a hard problem — and where they must fail. No-go proofs count because they tell searchers to quit dead ends. This one is for experts in hard-problem theory.
arxiv-2606-16070: Games like poker hide information — you can't see your opponent's cards. Mind-Studio builds "executable world models" for such partially observable games: simulations the AI can run forward, with lookahead evaluation to judge future moves. The paper shows how planning inside a learned model helps AI play games with hidden information.
arxiv-2606-16470: Telling a robot what to do from video requires understanding objects, not just pixels. This paper decouples object-centric video understanding from command generation: first parse the scene into objects, then produce manipulation commands for the robot. It targets robotics researchers connecting vision to action.
arxiv-2606-16870: To fake a cracking cookie on screen, you need the true stuff-feel of dough. This paper works back from the look: hidden-space RL finds what stuff-feel makes the break look true. It is for screen-food artists. Crack it right, on screen.
